items.expected-result: `serve --port 0` binds and reports its port; `serve --restart` on that port cycles the server it finds rather than attaching, and never touches port 7721
items.evidence: [650] asking the server on port 50878 to stop (pid 74614, 1.20.1+8f644051...) -> [651] the server on port 50878 (pid 74614) stopped and the port is free -> Now listening on: http://127.0.0.1:50878 (new pid 75108). ps -p 74614 empty; ps -p 75108 alive; curl :50878/mcp -> 401.
items.observed-result: Genuine cycle on a non-default ephemeral port: old pid gone, same port rebound under a new pid, server answering. Edge case recorded: `--restart --port 0` does NOT cycle, because each ephemeral pick is unrelated, so restart correctly falls back to a plain start per its documented behaviour. Expected, not a defect; the item was retested by passing the actual bound port.
items.acceptance-reason: Verified from live process state and live HTTP, not log text alone. The --port 0 edge case was explained rather than presented as the cycle test.

items.expected-result: memory_write returns a hash for a stored entry; a rejected write returns Stored=false with a reason and no fabricated hash (ADR-0032)
items.command: memory_write (valid) then memory_write with the Hermes background-process-log signature
items.observed-result: Both halves of ADR-0032 hold: a real write returns a real hash; a rejected write returns stored=false with EMPTY hash and path and a reason naming the exact policy — no fabricated identity. Reason string matches the ADR's specified format verbatim.
items.acceptance-reason: Truthful store and truthful rejection both exercised live. A write-only check would have passed whether or not truthful reporting works.

items.expected-result: memory_search returns the written entry through hybrid BM25 + vector RRF ranking
items.command: memory_write 'An astrolabe rests on the observatory shelf, glinting under warm lamplight...'; memory_search query='an antique navigation instrument reflecting evening light in a stargazing room'
items.evidence: {"hash":"88162269eff1...","ranking":1,"snippet":"An astrolabe rests on the observatory shelf..."}
items.observed-result: Query shares ZERO non-stopword tokens with the stored content, so BM25/FTS cannot explain the hit — only the vector leg bridges astrolabe->antique navigation instrument and observatory->stargazing room. Top and only result.
items.acceptance-reason: Query deliberately built with no literal overlap per the skill's guidance; a keyword-only engine returns nothing here. This is the form of the item that can actually fail.

items.expected-result: memory_get returns the full entry for a hash reachable from the caller; an unknown hash refuses rather than returning empty (ADR-0035)
items.evidence: {"value":"An astrolabe rests on the observatory shelf, glinting under warm lamplight it caught after dusk.","context":"project:laneB-item2"}
items.observed-result: Returned the exact original content byte-for-byte for the hash written moments earlier (ADR-0035).
items.acceptance-reason: Hash round-trip against a real write, content matches verbatim.

items.why-this-item-exists: Derived for this run, not in the template: WP1 (ADR-0075) makes a bank open skip the entire ~39-statement Ddl block when PRAGMA application_id matches a digest of Ddl. That is the single highest-blast-radius change in this build and no automated test exercises it through a real install. Lane B flagged it as uncovered rather than fabricating a result.
items.command: start server on fresh --data-root/--port 0, write an entry, read PRAGMA application_id/user_version read-only, cycle the process with `serve --port <bound> --restart`, then search/get/write through the NEW process
items.evidence: PRAGMA application_id=1230295233 (non-zero: digest stamped), user_version=10. Restart: [650] stop -> [651] port free -> Now listening on 127.0.0.1:52931, pid 85595 -> 86309. After reopen: semantic search 'a clockwork model of the solar system in a lobby lit by daylight' -> hash 418197a63e06, snippet 'A brass orrery turns slowly in the planetarium foyer...'; memory_get -> full original value; new memory_write -> stored=true.
items.observed-result: A bank whose Ddl block is skipped entirely on open still reads by hash, retrieves semantically, and accepts new writes. The digest is stamped and matches, so the fast path was genuinely taken rather than the bank falling back to a full Ddl rerun.
items.acceptance-reason: The search query shares no literal tokens with the stored text, so the vector leg is proven live AFTER the reopen — not merely that the file opened. Digest stamp read directly from the bank read-only, confirming the fast path applied rather than assuming it.
